routes.label: Use opposite angles in the circle

question:
In the given circle, the diameter \(\overline{EB}\) is parallel to \(\overline{DC},\) and \(\overline{AB}\) is parallel to \(\overline{ED}.\) The angles \(AEB\) and \(ABE\) are in the ratio \(4 : 5.\) What is the degree measure of angle \(BCD?\)

[Figure 1](figures/2011_AMC_10B_Q17_question_fig1.svg)
solution:
The diameter \(EB\) gives a right angle in triangle \(AEB\), allowing us to turn the given ratio into exact angles. Since \(A\) lies on the circle,
\[
\angle EAB=90^\circ.
\]
Thus \(\angle AEB+\angle ABE=90^\circ\). Their ratio is \(4:5\), so each of the nine equal parts measures \(90^\circ/9=10^\circ\). Therefore
\[
\angle AEB=40^\circ,\qquad
\angle ABE=50^\circ.
\]
Because \(AB\parallel ED\), the transversal \(EB\) gives equal alternate interior angles:
\[
\angle BED=\angle ABE=50^\circ.
\]
The points \(B,C,D,E\) lie on the same circle in that order. Hence \(BCDE\) is a cyclic quadrilateral, whose opposite angles at \(E\) and \(C\) sum to \(180^\circ\). It follows that
\[
\angle BCD=180^\circ-50^\circ
=\boxed{130^\circ},
\]
which is choice \(\boxed{\text{C}}\).
